source_caption:
🎬 Bob Hearts Abishola (2019–2024)

Bob Hearts Abishola follows Bob Wheeler, a hardworking and successful businessman from Detroit whose life takes an unexpected turn when he suffers a heart attack and falls in love with Abishola Adebambo, a compassionate Nigerian nurse who helps care for him during his recovery. Despite their completely different backgrounds, personalities, and cultural traditions, Bob becomes determined to win Abishola’s heart and build a meaningful relationship with her. Abishola is a hardworking single mother raising her son Dele while balancing her demanding nursing career, family responsibilities, and the expectations of her traditional Nigerian relatives. Meanwhile, Bob manages his family’s successful sock business while dealing with his outspoken mother Dottie and his unpredictable siblings. From awkward romantic encounters and hilarious cultural misunderstandings to complicated family disagreements, workplace challenges, and unexpected relationship struggles, Bob and Abishola discover that love requires patience, understanding, and compromise. As their relationship develops, their families gradually become connected, creating countless funny and heartfelt moments that challenge their beliefs and traditions. Combining warmhearted comedy, relatable family struggles, memorable characters, and meaningful cultural storytelling, the series explores love, family, immigration, friendship, acceptance, and the unexpected ways people from different worlds can find happiness together.

🎭 Genre: Sitcom • Comedy • Romance • Family

⭐ IMDb: 7.1/10

⏱️ Runtime: 22 minutes per episode • TV-PG

🎥 Creators: Chuck Lorre, Eddie Gorodetsky, Al Higgins & Gina Yashere

📺 Where to Watch: Check Paramount+, Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, and Fandango at Home for current streaming or digital purchase availability. Availability varies by region.

source_details.synopsis: Bob Hearts Abishola (stylized as Bob ♡ Abishola) is an American television sitcom created by Chuck Lorre, Eddie Gorodetsky, Al Higgins, and Gina Yashere that ran on CBS from September 23, 2019, to May 6, 2024, lasting five seasons and 95 episodes. It stars Billy Gardell and Folake Olowofoyeku as the respective titular characters, with Christine Ebersole, Matt Jones, Maribeth Monroe, Shola Adewusi, Barry Shabaka Henley, Travis Wolfe Jr., Vernee Watson, Bayo Akinfemi, Anthony Okungbowa, Saidah Arrika Ekulona, and Gina Yashere in supporting roles.
